A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoS framework and retain substantial shared experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original movie-personalization user-study results, BBQ and IAT experiments, and implicit-hate classification and quantification results, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds personalization comparisons, multi-context demonstrations, OpenbookQA experiments, Wikipedia continuations, and LaMP tweet-paraphrasing results.

M1.justification: The single-context decoding rule in Eq. (3) remains. However, v2 introduces independently weighted multiple contexts combined around prompt-only logits in Appendix B, and paired-context contrasts for inverse inference in Section 2.3. These extend the procedure beyond v1's single-context formulation.

E1.justification: V2 adds personalization in travel, wellness, learning, and cooking; OpenbookQA factuality evaluation; Wikipedia continuation under different requested formats; and LaMP tweet paraphrasing. It also introduces political/dietary inference examples and conflicting/non-conflicting multiple-context scenarios. The original movie, STEM, bias, and hate-speech coverage remains.

E2.justification: V1's personalization comparisons primarily vary CoS against no-context and ordinary context-prepending settings. V2 Section 3.1 and Figure 4 add evaluated one-demonstration in-context learning and iterative multi-turn personalization methods. The existing hate-speech LLM/human comparisons and bias-model comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The reported movie-study sample changes from 8 to 15 participants, retaining 70 responses per participant. V2 adds GPT-4 pairwise evaluation, timing per character, held-out calibration for personalization comparisons, and new ROUGE/coherence/diversity protocols. LaMP explicitly selects lambda values using training data and evaluates held-out data; these reports do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds context-position sensitivity, factuality under irrelevant/false/long contexts, negative-lambda contrasts, coherence/diversity checks, and multiple-context interaction studies. Its multidomain stability analysis replaces v1's extensive toddler-example lambda sweep. Existing IAT refusal and disambiguated-BBQ analyses remain in the appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the personalization Spearman analysis, hate-rating significance result, 40 generations per IAT prompt, and five GPT-3.5 ratings per personalization prompt. No new seed, confidence-interval, repeated-run, or significance-testing practice is documented. The participant-count revision concerns evaluation sample size.

E6.justification: V2 adds baseline win rates and timing, factuality and generation-quality results, and LaMP scores. For example, its new LaMP evaluation reports ROUGE-1/L of 0.42/0.36 at lambda=-0.5 versus 0.39/0.33 at lambda=0. Retained hate-classification accuracies remain 82%, 47%, and 60.5%; the additions are not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds a multi-context mathematical definition and order-invariance rationale, computational-complexity expressions, and a probability-ratio interpretation. These are limited formal extensions without new proofs. The added probability-ratio expression in Section 2.2 disagrees with the retained Eq. (3) at lambda=0.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds a unified contribution to personalization, debiasing, and hate quantification. V2 centers controllable personalization and open-ended tone/intent inference, and adds a main claim of more reliable control than turn-based and prompt-based methods. Debiasing remains supported but is no longer a headline contribution in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of topic confounding in inverse inference, why negative lambda need not reverse meaning, and why attenuating irrelevant context can help LaMP. It discusses unequal influence between simultaneous contexts and computational tradeoffs. Its composability limitation narrows to controlling multiple input regions, and stability guidance becomes explicitly case-dependent.

D1.justification: Appendix A changes the code-release statement from future availability to reported public availability. V2 additionally documents experimental prompts, lambda grids, 100-character inputs and 512-token continuation limits, and temperature 0.6 for stability examples. These extend reproducibility information without establishing changes to retained experiments' implementation.

R1.justification: The principal comparisons with activation steering, contrastive decoding, and training-based debiasing remain. V2 adds references on personalization and recommender alignment, contrastive reasoning, GPT-based evaluation, and the new benchmarks and metrics. The debiasing literature discussion is shortened, with its main cited approaches retained.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, and inverse-model explanation. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, the main bias experiment moves to Appendix F, and a new Additional Studies section reorganizes the narrative around personalization and applicability. This exceeds routine wording and numbering edits.

P2.justification: The overview diagram moves to the first page, and the main inference illustration changes to dietary/political posterior plots; the broader original STEM illustration survives in Appendix E. V2 adds baseline/runtime/radar plots, multiple-context grids, robustness figures, and benchmark tables. Bias displays move into the appendices, with substantial accompanying layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence about comparative personalization performance and output-quality tradeoffs. Figure 4 evaluates competing personalization procedures and computational cost, while Appendix C tests factuality, generation quality, and benchmark personalization, including cases where attenuating context works better. These strengthen assessment of the central method. The added probability formula's inconsistent lambda convention and incomplete documentation of new evaluations weaken formal clarity and reproducibility, but do not outweigh the substantive empirical gains.
